--- title: "Get row as dicitonary from polars dataframe" subtitle: "row" author: '{{< var author >}}' date: '2025-10-21' date-format: iso toc: true toc-title: 'Sections' toc-location: right toc-depth: 3 categories: [100DaysOfPolars] --- The Polars dataframe is highly accessible. In fact, you can get a row as a dictionary and use it directly in your Python code. Below is a dataframe showing clothing brands. ::: {#1b9e5547 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Get row as dictionary To get the second row as a dictionary from a Polars dataframe, you use the `row` method as like this: ::: {#0dc5a748 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} (df .row(2, named=True) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'Brand': 'Forever21', 'Category': 'Basic', 'Price': 39} ``` ::: ::: You now have a dictionary where the keys are column names and the values are the corresponding row values.
